executiveSummary: RUN-D (Vanilla) scored 99/100. RUN-E (v0.4 Factory Lite Core) scored 95/100. The 4-point difference is entirely attributable to UI implementation depth (D09: 5 vs 2). Without UI, scores would be 94 vs 93 — statistically identical. v0.4 Factory Lite Core mechanisms did NOT produce a measurable product quality improvement over Vanilla Codex for the LedgerFlow Lite benchmark.

generalizabilityAssessment.acrossTwoBenchmarks: With EVAL-8 (first benchmark) and EVAL-13 (LedgerFlow), v0.4 has now been tested on two benchmarks. EVAL-8 showed Factory Lite Core underperforming (55 vs 88). EVAL-13 shows a closer result (95 vs 99) but still no measurable product quality advantage.
generalizabilityAssessment.consistentFinding: Across both benchmarks, v0.4 Factory Lite Core mechanisms provide PROCESS-LEVEL benefits (audit trail, contamination control, anti-gaming) but do not consistently produce PRODUCT-LEVEL quality improvements over Vanilla Codex.
caveats: RUN-E used sql.js (WASM) due to environmental constraint — this is not a v0.4 design choice
RUN-E's minimal UI may reflect anti-overengineering rules working as designed
RUN-D's UI richness required more code (22 files vs 12) — complexity vs quality tradeoff
Two benchmarks is limited evidence. More benchmarks needed for robust generalizability claim.

recommendationOptions.reason: Evidence does not support clear v0.4 advantage. Two benchmarks show v0.4 Core does not improve product quality. Releasing v0.4 as 'improves quality' would be misleading.

The 3-role optional model was deferred. Testing whether Architect+Builder+Reviewer adds value (especially for UI quality) is the logical next question. RUN-E's UI gap might be addressed by a dedicated reviewer role.

v0.4 draft could benefit from: (1) clearer guidance on when UI investment is appropriate despite anti-overengineering, (2) recognition that process mechanisms ≠ product quality, (3) framing v0.4 as 'process integrity layer' rather than 'quality improvement layer'
Two benchmarks is limited evidence. Third benchmark with different project type would strengthen conclusions.
Mixed evidence. User should decide direction based on their priorities: process integrity vs product quality vs role model testing.

verdictRationale: Product quality scores are effectively identical when controlling for UI (94 vs 93)
The 4-point gap favoring Vanilla is in UI depth, not in core functionality
v0.4's unique contributions (POR, evidence hierarchy, anti-gaming) are evaluation-integrity tools, not product-quality tools
The anti-overengineering rules in the Constitution may have actively suppressed UI investment in RUN-E
Process overhead (~375ms) is negligible and non-disruptive
No blockers found in either run
